topIssues.title: kona-genesis: RollupConfig silently accepts unknown rollup.json keys
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Summary

Kona's [`RollupConfig`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/protocol/genesis/src/rollup.rs#L34-L37) carries no `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, so any key in a `rollup.json` that kona does not model is silently dropped. [`test_rollup_config_unknown_field`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/protocol/genesis/src/rollup.rs#L992-L1048) pins that behaviour as intended.

The rollup config is the chain's consensus-parameter file. A key kona ignores is a parameter kona does not honour: `kona-node` / `kona-host` boot happily on a config that tells them to derive a chain different from the one the operator configured, and the disagreement only shows up later as a derivation split or a failed proof.

## Why it matters

`rollup.json` is produced by op-deployer from Go's [`rollup.Config`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/op-node/rollup/types.go#L87-L195) (`DeployConfig.RollupConfig`). Today every key that struct emits is modelled by kona, so nothing is being dropped in practice. The gap is the *next* consensus field: op-node adds it, op-deployer writes it, op-node honours it, and kona-node ignores it and derives a different chain — with no error anywhere.

Kona already applies exactly this guard on the *other* rollup-config ingestion path, the superchain-registry one: both [`ChainConfig`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/protocol/genesis/src/chain/config.rs#L33-L37) and [`HardForkConfig`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/protocol/genesis/src/chain/hardfork.rs#L10-L14) are `deny_unknown_fields`, and [`docs/ai/derivation.md`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/docs/ai/derivation.md#L63-L71) names strict decoding as one of the two guards that make an unwired config field fail loudly. The direct `rollup.json` path — which is what every non-registry chain actually uses — has no such guard.

Note that op-node's [`ParseRollupConfig`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/op-node/rollup/types.go#L928-L934) is a plain `json.Decoder` and is lenient too, so this is not a kona-vs-op-node divergence today; it is a missing guard on both. Making op-node strict is not free — kona's own serialization emits keys op-node does not model (`granite_channel_timeout`, `superchain_config_address`, `blobs_data`, top-level `da_challenge_address`), so a strict op-node would reject a kona-written config. Kona is the side that can tighten without breaking an existing producer.

## The `flatten` wrinkle

`RollupConfig` flattens `HardForkConfig`:

```rust
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(flatten))]
pub hardforks: HardForkConfig,
```

Two things follow, both worth recording because serde's own documentation says `deny_unknown_fields` "is not supported in combination with flatten, neither on the outer struct nor on the flattened field":

1. `HardForkConfig`'s **own** `deny_unknown_fields` is inert once flattened. `FlatStructAccess` only picks the keys the struct declares and skips the rest, so the inner attribute never fires. That is why the unknown key in the test above is accepted today despite `HardForkConfig` being strict.
2. `deny_unknown_fields` on the **outer** struct does work, contrary to the doc note. `serde_derive` emits a leftover check after every flattened field has taken its own keys (`collected_deny_unknown_fields` in `serde_derive/src/de/struct_.rs`), so the flattened hardfork keys still parse and anything left over is a hard error. Verified against the pinned `serde_derive` 1.0.228, and present as far back as 1.0.145. The doc note holds only for a flattened catch-all *map*, which swallows everything and leaves nothing to check.

So no custom `Deserialize` or restructuring is needed, and the serialized `rollup.json` format is untouched.

## Proposed fix

- Add `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` to `RollupConfig`.
- Flip `test_rollup_config_unknown_field` to assert rejection.
- Add a fixture test that every key op-node can emit parses, generated from a fully-populated `rollup.Config` by a Go test that fails when the two drift apart.

## Compatibility

A `rollup.json` from a future op-deployer carrying a key kona does not model will fail to load on kona-node / kona-host with `unknown field <key>` instead of booting and quietly ignoring it. That is the intended trade: an operator sees a startup error rather than a chain that derives differently. All 25 keys op-node emits today are modelled, so no config produced by current tooling is affected.

## Related gap (out of scope here)

`BaseFeeConfig` (`chain_op_config`) is not `deny_unknown_fields`, so an unknown key nested inside it is still ignored. `ChainGenesis`, `SystemConfig` and `AltDAConfig` are all strict already.

topIssues.title: op-supernode: cross-safe wedges after invalid-message replacement while local-safe on one chain stalls
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
## Description

During recovery from an invalid-message replacement, the supernode's cross-safe head can wedge entirely: in CircleCI build [5418160](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/jobs/5418160) (merge queue, 2026-08-03, `memory-all-opn-op-reth-prague`), cross-safe on **both** chains stayed pinned at block 26 for the remainder of a 259s test run while chain 902's local-safe advanced to 125+ and unsafe sequencing continued to ~128. Surfaced as a failure of `TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement` (`ResendUntilSafe`: "transaction did not reach the safe chain within the resend budget") — but the resend budget is not the problem: with cross-safe frozen, no transaction could ever reach the EL's safe label. Split out of #22234, which retains the full flake analysis (its other two occurrences were a test-side read race, fixed by #22321).

## Evidence (log tail, 18:45:05–18:45:25)

State per chain, stable across the whole captured window:

| | chain 901 | chain 902 |
|---|---|---|
| local-safe (supernode) | **27** — stalled | **125** — advancing |
| cross-safe (supernode) | **26** — pinned | **26** — pinned |
| light CL unsafe | ~128 | ~128 |

The supernode logs this once per second, for the same block, the entire window (27 hits across both chains in the 20s tail):

```
engine_controller.go:1250: ERROR [08-03|18:45:05.335] Block must be safe before it can be finalized component=supernode chain_id=901 vn_id=a7bc ref=c7d5bb..1c44dd:27 safe=587d29..87b357:26
engine_controller.go:1250: ERROR [08-03|18:45:06.338] Block must be safe before it can be finalized component=supernode chain_id=902 vn_id=ed3a ref=6244e8..c88e5c:56 safe=079e41..081150:26
...
engine_controller.go:1250: ERROR [08-03|18:45:25.335] Block must be safe before it can be finalized component=supernode chain_id=901 vn_id=a7bc ref=c7d5bb..1c44dd:27 safe=587d29..87b357:26
```

Meanwhile the light follow-CLs keep force-resetting and re-adopting the frozen upstream view every ~4s (#21119 oscillation), e.g.:

```
engine_controller.go:1325: INFO [08-03|18:45:23.152] Reset of Engine is completed component=l2cl-sequencer local_unsafe=c7d5bb..1c44dd:27 cross_unsafe=c7d5bb..1c44dd:27 local_safe=c7d5bb..1c44dd:27 cross_safe=587d29..87b357:26
engine_controller.go:1325: INFO [08-03|18:45:23.205] Reset of Engine is completed component=l2cl-sequencer local_unsafe=ae8666..786002:125 cross_unsafe=ae8666..786002:125 local_safe=ae8666..786002:125 cross_safe=079e41..081150:26
```

Timeline context: the test's earlier gates all passed — `AwaitValidatedTimestamp` for the replacement, and cross-safe advanced 3 blocks past it (to 26) — and *then* cross-safe stopped for 100+ blocks of subsequent chain activity.

## Reading

- Chain 901's **local-safe derivation stalled at 27** (the invalid message was on chain 902; 901 was the initiating chain). Since cross-safe promotion advances the two chains' frontiers together, 901's stall plausibly pins cross-safe at 26 on both chains, including 902 whose own local-safe is healthy at 125.
- The recurring `Block must be safe before it can be finalized` error shows the finalization path repeatedly attempting to finalize a block ahead of the cross-safe head — symptom or contributor, unclear.
- The resent transactions were plain ETH transfers (no interop messages), so cross-validation had no legitimate dependency to wait on at those heights.

Open questions: why did 901's local-safe stop at 27 — batcher stopped batching 901, derivation wedged post-replacement, or supervisor-side databases inconsistent after the replacement? And is the once-per-second finalization error loop masking or causing the missed promotion?

Only the last ~20s of the run's logs are captured in the CI step output; a local repro with supervisor debug logging would show when 901's local-safe stopped relative to the replacement.

## Why it matters

If reproducible outside the test, this is a liveness failure: a chain pair that goes through interop invalid-message replacement stops advancing cross-safe (and therefore safe/finalized) indefinitely, while unsafe sequencing keeps running. #20134 was a similar-looking cross-safe stall with a different trigger (deep L1 reorg) and is closed.

## Related

- #22234 — flake tracking + full analysis of all three test failures
- #22321 — fixes the other (test-side) failure signature
- #21119 — light follow path forceReset oscillation (background noise in the same logs)

topIssues.title: l1-watcher: a transient L1 RPC failure on one chain kills the whole node
topIssues.author: claude
topIssues.body:
In the kona-node L1 watcher, one chain's failure is fatal to the whole node. When a chain's `eth_getLogs` request for system config logs fails — a transient L1 RPC error is enough — or a chain's derivation channel is closed, `L1WatcherActor::step` (`rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/actors/l1_watcher/actor.rs`) returns `Err`. The actor runner at `rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/service/util.rs:33` treats any actor error as fatal: it cancels every actor, and the host exits.

This predates the multi-chain watcher change in #22567 — a single-chain kona-node dies the same way when its L1 RPC hiccups, and transient L1 failures should never kill the node. At N > 1 chains served by one watcher the blast radius grows: one chain's transient L1 error stops every other chain in the host.

From the review discussion on #22567 (https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22567#discussion_r3838547816):

> Indeed this seems like a bug in even the current kona-node because transient L1 failures should never kill the node. We should log an issue for this and then create a follow up PR to fix it properly.

A follow-up PR will add per-chain fault handling: transient RPC errors retried or skipped rather than propagated as fatal, and per-chain isolation so one chain's failure does not stop the others.

Part of #22531.

topIssues.title: kona-node: sequencer stuck in forkchoiceUpdated -38002 loop after derivation force-includes a block off its unsafe chain
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
A kona-node **sequencer** can be permanently wedged — hot-looping `engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV3` at thousands of calls per second until the process is unusable — whenever the engine reorgs its unsafe head while the sequencer has a block build in flight. Derivation force-inclusion after a batcher outage makes that reorg happen deterministically, so a sequencing-window expiry reliably kills the node.

Two independent defects combine:

1. `BuildTask` classifies a `-38002 Invalid forkchoice state` response as a **temporary** error, and the task queue retries temporary errors in an unbounded loop with no backoff. The condition is not transient, so the node never leaves the loop and never resets.
2. `BuildTask` has no staleness guard on the parent it was asked to build on, so it will send the EL a forkchoice state whose `safeBlockHash` is not an ancestor of `headBlockHash` in the first place.

All references below are against `68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327`.

## Observed

On a devnet running a kona-node sequencer + kona-node verifier + batcher (a multi-block PoC branch, #22671 — but nothing in the mechanism is specific to it):

- The batcher submitted batches derivation could not apply.
- The sequencing window expired, so derivation force-included an empty block at height `N+1` whose parent was the last common block `N`, but whose hash differed from the sequencer's own unsafe block at `N+1`.
- The node then emitted `engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV3` → `-38002 Invalid forkchoice state` in a hot loop, thousands per second, until it was dead. It never reorged its unsafe chain onto the derived chain and never recovered.

## Mechanism

**Step 1 — derivation reorgs the unsafe chain (this part works).** The derived attributes for `N+1` fail the consolidation check against the sequencer's block at `N+1`, so [`ConsolidateTask`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/consolidate/task.rs#L271-L281) falls back to `build_and_seal`, and the [`InsertTask`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/insert/task.rs#L98-L110) that finishes it sets `unsafe_head`, `local_safe_head` and `safe_head` to the derived block. The EL and the engine state both end up on the derived chain.

**Step 2 — the sequencer submits a build against the pre-reorg head.** `SequencerActor::build_unsealed_payload` reads the unsafe head from a watch channel *once*, at [actor.rs#L217](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/actors/sequencer/actor.rs#L217), then does two pieces of network-bound async work (L1 origin selection, then `prepare_payload_attributes`, which fetches L1 receipts) before [submitting the build at L246](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/actors/sequencer/actor.rs#L245-L246). The `EngineActor` republishes the unsafe head only at the top of its step loop, [after draining the queue](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/actors/engine/actor.rs#L224-L231). So the snapshot the sequencer built against is routinely stale by the time the request lands — a window of hundreds of milliseconds, and the step-1 reorg falls squarely inside it.

**Step 3 — the FCU is rejected.** [`BuildTask::start_build`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/build/task.rs#L104-L110) overrides only the head with the attributes' parent and keeps the state's `safe_head`:

```rust
let new_forkchoice = state
    .sync_state
    .apply_update(EngineSyncStateUpdate { unsafe_head: Some(attributes_envelope.parent), ..Default::default() })
    .create_forkchoice_state();
```

`head = <pre-reorg sequencer block>`, `safe = <derived block>`. The derived block is not an ancestor of the pre-reorg head, so the EL answers `-38002`.

**Step 4 — the hot loop.** `-38002` arrives as a JSON-RPC error and is mapped unconditionally to [`EngineBuildError::AttributesInsertionFailed`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/build/task.rs#L132), which carries severity [`Temporary`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/build/error.rs#L62-L68). `EngineTask::execute` retries temporary errors [in a `while let Err(..)` loop whose only pause is `yield_now().await`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/task.rs#L216-L231) — no backoff, no attempt cap. The forkchoice state is a function of engine state that nothing else can change while the queue is draining, so the retry can never succeed. That is the thousands-of-FCUs-per-second symptom.

**Step 5 — total wedge.** The loop lives inside `Engine::drain`, which the `EngineActor` runs *before* receiving its next request, so the actor can no longer process anything — including a `Reset` request. Meanwhile the sequencer is parked in `start_build_block` awaiting a payload id that will never arrive, so it cannot ask for that reset either. Nothing in the process can break the cycle.

Note the asymmetry that makes this a plain bug rather than a design trade-off: the attribute-less forkchoice update in `SynchronizeTask` **does** special-case the same error code, mapping it to [`SynchronizeTaskError::InvalidForkchoiceState`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/synchronize/task.rs#L125-L135) with severity `Reset`. Only the build path is missing it.

## op-node comparison

op-node guards the same two points, and this is where the fix comes from.

- **Stale parent.** [`EngineController.startBuild`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/op-node/rollup/engine/build_start.go#L57-L65) refuses a sequencer build whose parent is not the current unsafe head, before any engine call:

  ```go
  if !attrs.IsDerived() && attrs.Parent.ID() != e.unsafeHead.ID() {
      e.log.Warn("dropping stale sequencer build start", ...)
      e.requestForkchoiceUpdate(ctx)   // sequencer restarts on the current unsafe head
      return nil, ErrStaleBuild
  }
  ```

  The `!attrs.IsDerived()` condition matters: a derivation-driven reorg legitimately builds on a parent that differs from the unsafe head.

- **`-38002` from the pre-block-creation FCU.** [`startPayload`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go#L1476-L1483) classifies it as `BlockInsertPrestateErr` — "pre-block-creation forkchoice update was inconsistent with engine, need reset to resolve" — which `startBuild` turns into a [`ResetEvent`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/op-node/rollup/engine/build_start.go#L104-L109), never a retry.

op-node has also already been bitten by the adjacent oscillation: see the `#21119` comment in [`FollowSource`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go#L1578-L1590) — "head on the fork, safe on upstream -> InvalidForkchoiceState -> reset re-selects the fork -> oscillation" — fixed there with a `forceReset` that lands head and safe in one shot.

## Proposed fix

1. Map `-38002` in `BuildTask::start_build` to a new `EngineBuildError::InvalidForkchoiceState` with severity `Reset`, mirroring `SynchronizeTask` and op-node's `startPayload`.
2. Give `BuildTask` op-node's stale-parent guard, gated on the existing `BuildSealCoupling` flag that `SealTask` already uses for exactly this distinction (`Atomic` = derivation-driven, parent chosen from engine state, skip the check; `Detached` = external caller working from its own snapshot, check it). Report the rejection to the caller over the result channel instead of leaving it waiting.
3. Have the sequencer treat a rejected or dropped build as "re-build on the new head next tick" rather than a fatal actor error — every `NodeActor::step` error [shuts the whole node down](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/service/util.rs#L28-L38).
4. Publish the unsafe head after an engine reset as well, so the sequencer cannot build against a pre-reset snapshot.

Worth considering separately, not covered by the above: the task queue's temporary-error retry has no backoff at all. Any genuinely temporary engine error currently spins the engine as fast as the EL will answer. op-node's equivalent yields to a driver that re-attempts on a timer.

## Repro status

Not reproduced as an automated test. The Rust-side mechanism is covered by unit tests in the fix PR (a `-38002` build must surface as `Reset` and must not be retried; a stale detached build must be rejected without touching the engine; the sequencer must retry rather than die). A full-system repro is blocked on a harness gap:

- **No test anywhere exercises batcher outage → sequencing-window expiry → force-include → sequencer unsafe-chain reorg against a kona-node sequencer.** Not in `op-acceptance-tests/`, not in `rust/kona/tests/node/`, not in Rust.
- The one test that models the whole loop end-to-end, `TestSequencingWindowExpiry` (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/seqwindow/expiry_test.go`), is bound to `presets.NewTwoL2SupernodeInterop`. Supernode presets never route through `startL2CLForKey`, so they have no `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND` branch and cannot start a `KonaNode`.
- Every op-e2e action test that asserts force-inclusion or post-expiry recovery (`TestL2Verifier_SequenceWindow`, `TestL2Sequencer_SequencerOnlyReorg`, `ExtendedTimeWithoutL1Batches`, `DeepReorg`) drives the in-process Go `L2Sequencer` object directly. There is no engine-API boundary to swap, so they can never target an external CL process. `rust/kona/tests/proofs/sequence_window_expiry_test.go` describes exactly this scenario but its sequencer is op-node — kona only appears there as `kona-host`.
- `rust/kona/tests/node/` has no derivation-stress package (`node/common`, `node/reorgs`, `node/restart`), and `NewMixedOpKona`/`NewMixedOpKonaForConfig` do not accept deployer options, so that preset cannot set a small `sequencerWindowSize` without a signature change.

The gap is fillable: `presets.NewMinimal(t, presets.WithDeployerOptions(sysgo.WithSequencingWindow(N)))` is accepted by the minimal preset, `startL2CLForKey` honours `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND=kona-node`, and the whole acceptance suite already runs against kona-node in the required `memory-all-kona-op-reth-fusaka` CI job. `dsl.L2Batcher.Stop()/Start()` and `dsl.L2CLNode.SetSequencerRecoverMode` all exist and kona implements `admin_setRecoverMode`. What is missing is the test itself. One risk worth flagging for whoever writes it: kona's derivation is gated behind EL-sync completion, which only completes after a P2P-delivered unsafe payload (see the note at `op-acceptance-tests/tests/sdm/init_test.go`).

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5*

topIssues.title: [PCD] Default-`X` benchmarking
topIssues.author: 0xOneTony
topIssues.body: `X` (the offset between the chosen L1 anchor's timestamp and the committed L2 `genesis_time`) must be large enough that `genesis_time` is still in the future when `OPCM.deploy()` is mined; otherwise `op-node` will produce empty filler blocks at L2 block time to fill the gap. Measure end-to-end runtime of the off-chain portion of the pipeline (anchor selection through prestate generation) against a real prestate builder, repeated enough times to get a stable result. Propose a default `X`.

topPRs.title: Silhouette: private interoperable chains (v1, attested)
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
## Silhouette: private interoperable chains (v1, attested) A silhouette chain is a private L2 that participates in an ordinary interop dependency set. Its transactions stay private. L1 carries a signed proof envelope describing the chain's public outline and a standard derivation carrier with user transactions removed. v1 is explicitly operator-attested: the trusted submitter's L1 signature authenticates the claimed state. The wire reserves a proof slot for a future proven mode, but this PR contains no ZK toolchain or L1 settlement path. ### Architecture - **No `op-node` changes.** The final PR diff under `op-node/` is empty. - **No custom submitter.** The normal `op-batcher` loads real private blocks, receipts and output roots and retains its normal channel, reorg, txmgr and retry lifecycle. A terminal encoder emits the silhouette proof envelope followed by standard carrier frames for the same block cadence with user transactions removed. - **Normal inbox and stock portal.** Both envelope and carrier go to the rollup's normal batch inbox. Deposits remain enabled and are stock-derived; there is no gated portal contract. - **Stock derivation.** A stock verifier `op-node` ignores the `KCPB` proof blob as an unknown derivation format, consumes the following standard carrier frames, and runs the ordinary Holocene/interop rewind and deposits-only replacement path. - **One verifier-only supernode role.** Silhouette chains cannot be sequenced by a supernode virtual node. Private sequencing is performed by a LightCL op-node backed by the private EL. - **Standalone magic EL.** `op-silhouette-el` is an in-memory Engine/eth RPC service. It watches the authenticated proof stream independently, maps stock carrier attributes to proof-committed block hashes and roots, and delegates a stock deposits-only replacement build to the private EL when interop invalidates a proven block. - **Normal interop semantics.** The supernode's stock judge validates the private chain's declared imports against independently derived public-chain messages. Invalid blocks are replaced and transitive invalidation propagates across chains. ### What is posted to L1 Each normal batcher submission contains: 1. `KCPB` envelope magic, wire version, public-values length/data, and proof length/data (empty in attested mode). 2. Batch commitments: previous/new output root, L1 head hash, rollup-config hash, dependency-set hash, export-policy hash, and the block list. 3. Per block: number, timestamp, real block hash, state root, message-passer storage root, exported logs, imported messages, L1-origin hash/number, and sequence number. 4. Per exported log: real block log index, log hash, and optional preimage (empty under the default all-hashes policy). 5. Per imported message: origin, source block/log index/timestamp/chain ID, and payload hash. 6. Standard compressed derivation channel/frame data carrying each block's parent, epoch, timestamp, stock deposits/L1-info transaction, and an empty user-transaction list. It does **not** publish private user transaction bytes or hashes, senders, calldata, receipts, contract state, or full log contents. The ordinary L1 blob transaction still exposes its sender, destination inbox, nonce, fees, commitments and inclusion block. ### Images Build these three branch-specific targets: ```sh docker buildx bake op-batcher op-supernode op-silhouette-el ``` | Image | Difference from a normal interop deployment | |---|---| | `op-batcher` | Enables the terminal silhouette proof + stripped-carrier encoding. | | `op-supernode` | Loads the silhouette verifier manifest and proof observer. It remains verifier-only. | | `op-silhouette-el` | New in-memory proof-backed Engine/eth service used as P's verifier EL. | The standalone `op-node`, L1/L2 execution clients, and portal contracts are stock. There is no `proofbatch-submitter` image. ### Minimal configuration delta Private producer: ```sh op-batcher --data-availability-type blobs --silhouette \ --max-pending-tx 1 --target-num-frames 6 \ --silhouette.inbox $NORMAL_BATCH_INBOX --silhouette.wire-version 4 \ --silhouette.rollup-config-hash $ROLLUP_HASH \ --silhouette.dependency-set-hash $DEPSET_HASH ``` The producer is otherwise a normal LightCL sequencer + private EL. It uses the stock `OptimismPortal`; the silhouette inbox must equal the normal rollup batch inbox. Magic EL: ```sh op-silhouette-el --l1 $L1_RPC --l1.beacon $L1_BEACON \ --supernode $SUPERNODE_RPC --rollup-config rollup-p.json \ --verifier-config verifier-p.json \ --replacement-engine $PRIVATE_ENGINE_AUTH_RPC \ --replacement-engine.jwt-secret jwt.txt --rpc.addr 0.0.0.0 --rpc.port 9545 ``` Verifier supernode: ```sh op-supernode --silhouette manifest.json \ --vn.

.l2 http://op-silhouette-el:9545 \ --vn.

.interop.dependency-set depset.json ``` The `op-node` VN has no silhouette/private flag: its only unusual input is that its configured EL endpoint speaks the proof-backed Engine API. The manifest names P's verifier config; A is absent and remains an ordinary chain. The verifier config binds L1 chain ID, trusted submitter, normal inbox, rollup/dependency-set hashes, `proofType: "attested"`, `wireVersion: 4`, and the anchor. ### Local network and smoke tests ```sh go run ./op-up --silhouette # funded transactional RPCs: A http://127.0.0.1:8545, B http://127.0.0.1:8546 go run ./op-up smoke-interop all go run ./op-up smoke-interop invalid-message --direction both --reorg-timeout 5m go run ./op-up smoke-interop chained-invalid-message --require-cascade --reorg-timeout 5m # comparison topology go run ./op-up --interop ``` Observed locally on this revision: - silhouette `smoke-interop all`: PASS; - bidirectional invalid A→B and B→A: both replaced and both chains resumed; - strict chained invalidation: invalid P block, direct dependent, and descendant dependent all reorged while the independent control remained; - normal sysgo bidirectional invalid smoke: same replacement/resume semantics (lower latency because it does not wait for the proof-batch cadence); - focused `TestSilhouetteImportThatIsFalseIsReplaced`: PASS; - `op-batcher`, all `op-supernode`, sysgo/presets, smoke utility, and `op-up` unit suites: PASS. The serialized full silhouette acceptance package still has one known timeout in `TestSilhouetteCrossChainPinsThenAdvances`; the replacement regression and proof-slot refusal tests pass independently. ### Diff size Against the PR base: approximately **24.3k insertions / 1.45k deletions across 267 files**. Much of the file count is the existing cross-language fixture corpus. The architecture rewrite in the latest commit is **3,487 insertions / 7,004 deletions**: it deletes the custom submitter, sequencing-side silhouette role, custom portal, and op-node hook in favor of the stock paths above. Operational details and the exact trust statement live in `op-supernode/silhouette/docs/RUNNING-V1.md` and `TRUST-MODEL.md`.

topPRs.title: kona-node,op-reth,op-batcher: multi-blocks PoC (up to max_multi_blocks blocks per block time)
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
**Draft / PoC, work in progress — CI feedback only for now.**

Multi-blocks: keep `block_time`, allow the sequencer to build up to `max_multi_blocks` L2 blocks sharing one timestamp after a feature timestamp `multi_block_time` (≥ Karst, not a hardfork). Sealing policy is the builder's choice; consensus only bounds the group size. Chain consistency is parent-hash linkage.

Scope of the PoC: kona-node (sequencer + derivation), op-reth (EL), op-batcher (span batch v2), op-devstack + acceptance tests on a kona-node/op-reth-only devnet. op-node keeps rejecting span batch v2; interop, proofs, flashblocks and registry support are out of scope.

Landed so far (one commit per workstream):
- op-reth: `ts == parent.ts` accepted iff siblings are allowed at `ts`; builder seal policy flags; `engine_awaitPayloadReadyV1`
- kona: `multi_block_time`/`max_multi_blocks` config; `BatchType::SpanV2` = Delta span + `same_ts_bits` (bit 0 = sibling of the span's parent, so groups may straddle spans/channels)
- Go: rollup/deploy config, span batch v2 codec + `SpanChannelOut` switch, devstack options and DSL helpers, shared golden vectors

Still to come: kona derivation validity, kona sequencer slot loop, acceptance tests.

Judgement calls worth a look:
- the `min-build-time` policy only seals a payload that holds ≥ 1 user tx, so an idle sequencer still makes one block per block time
- straddling groups across span batches/channels is allowed (bit 0), instead of forcing the batcher to keep groups atomic across L1-driven channel closes
- `siblings_allowed` is false at *every* configured fork activation timestamp, which keeps the timestamp-only `is_first_<fork>_block` predicates correct for forks scheduled after activation

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: throttle ERC20 and ETH withdrawals
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds development-gated withdrawal throttling for whitelisted ERC20s and ETH using percentage-based token buckets.

- Supports `L1StandardBridge`, `OptimismPortal2`, and shared `ETHLockbox` custody.
- Uses live escrow balances, lazy exact fractional refill, and revert-on-exhaustion.
- Adds owner configuration/refresh APIs and monitoring events.
- Configures throttles through OPCM instructions behind `WITHDRAWAL_THROTTLE`.
- Centralizes accounting in a reusable two-slot packed `WithdrawalThrottle.State`.
- Conservatively saturates capacities above `uint128.max`.

Cold-path benchmarks measure throttle overhead at approximately 17.3k gas for ERC20 finalization and 14.9k gas for ETH finalization.

## Testing

Added coverage for refill precision, overflow boundaries, reconfiguration, live-stock changes, shared-lockbox behavior, OPCM configuration, storage writes, and cold-path gas benchmarks.

topPRs.title: op-reth,kona: implement sequencer-defined fees
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
## Description

Implement Sequencer-Defined Fees (SDF) at Lagoon. The sequencer selects `baseFeePerGas` through a pluggable policy, commits that selection in the trailing `PostExec` transaction, and validators reproduce execution from the committed fee without running producer policy.

This change:

- extends the unactivated version-1 `PostExec` payload with the selected base fee
- requires a trailing Lagoon commitment, including for empty refund sets
- wires fee selection and immutable per-payload caching through op-reth payload building
- uses selected-fee quotes in txpool, pending execution, and fee-related RPC paths
- validates Lagoon commitments on Engine API block import
- reproduces fallback commitments in Kona and preserves them in output artifacts
- applies selected fees during flashblock replay and reserves block space for the mandatory commitment
- updates public documentation and acceptance-test expectations

L1 data fees, operator fees, batch formats, and payload-attribute schemas are unchanged.

## Dependencies

- Depends on ethereum-optimism/reth#8. The Rust workspace is pinned to that PR's organization-owned branch revision while it is under review.
- Specification: ethereum-optimism/specs#934.
- Premium policy integration: ethereum-optimism/optimism-premium#222.

## Validation

Completed before opening this draft:

- full Go lint and Optimism Rust lint on the initial series
- targeted op-reth/Kona tests, including 41 Kona executor tests
- no-std checks and nightly formatting
- focused checks for consensus, Kona executor/driver, flashblocks, payload builder, and RPC against the public reth revision
- regression tests for Engine API commitment validation, Kona fallback transaction persistence, flashblock selected-fee execution, and block-size reservation

Final review, broader validation after the latest fixes, and CI follow-up are still in progress.

## Review notes

Earlier independent review findings about the Engine API validation path, Kona fallback artifacts, flashblock fees, historical fee history, fill-transaction defaults, and block-size accounting were addressed before this draft was opened.

Dismissed findings:

- Cached policy failures are intentional: a payload ID has one immutable policy resolution across retries.
- A `PostExec` version 2 is unnecessary because version 1 has not activated onchain.
- Extending op-geth is out of scope because Lagoon follows the op-geth support horizon.
- No span-batch format change is required; span batches already transport the transaction bytes.

topPRs.title: contracts: prototype L1-certified event relay
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
## Overview

This draft prototypes an L1-mediated, censorship-resistant slow path for L2 events and interop messages.

A source `CrossL2Inbox` asks a consensus `LocalLogOracle` precompile to verify a recent local log, then exports the certificate through the existing `L2ToL1MessagePasser`. After ordinary withdrawal proving/finalization, `L1EventRegistry` records the certificate and can force-deposit it into any destination portal authorized by the same `ETHLockbox`. The destination inbox caches it and can either expose generic event validation or execute a certified `SentMessage` in the same deposit.

The event must be exported within seven days. Once registered on L1, the certificate is durable and can be relayed after ordinary interop expiry.

## Security decisions

- L1 derives the source chain from the calling portal and authenticates `portal.l2Sender()` as the canonical `CrossL2Inbox`; source identity is never trusted from calldata.
- Source and destination portals must both be current members of the registry immutable `ETHLockbox` cluster.
- Destination imports authenticate the L1 registry through standard L1-to-L2 address aliasing.
- Certified execution emits `ExecutingCertifiedMessage`, not `ExecutingMessage`, so ordinary interop expiry/dependency hazard rules are not accidentally applied.
- Certificates bind the full existing `Identifier` and exact payload hash. Messenger replay protection remains authoritative.

## Included

- `ILocalLogOracle` execution-client boundary and reserved system address
- source export and destination certificate cache in `CrossL2Inbox`
- immutable `L1EventRegistry` with portal/lockbox/source-chain authentication
- generic `relayEvent` and one-deposit `relayMessage` paths
- ABI, storage-layout, and semver snapshots
- focused L1/L2 unit tests
- design note: `packages/contracts-bedrock/specs/event-certificates.md`

## Draft blockers / follow-ups

- Specify and implement deterministic historical receipt access in op-geth, op-reth, Kona, and fault-proof re-execution. An optional archival database lookup is not consensus-safe; the final design needs a state-committed history structure or explicit witnesses anchored to consensus state.
- Define precompile gas, receipt encoding, pruning, reorg, and exact boundary semantics.
- Update interop clients to classify `ExecutingCertifiedMessage` as L1-certified rather than an ordinary executing-message dependency.
- Add genesis/NUT/deployment/standard-validator wiring for the registry and inbox configuration.
- Add forced-deposit and withdrawal-finalization end-to-end coverage.
- For ETH bridge recovery, separately enforce a unique transfer ID and one terminal outcome across relay and refund paths. Event presence alone does not prove non-execution.
- Consider batched exports before production use.

## Verification

- `mise x -- just build` (passes; one pre-existing payable-fallback warning in `L2ContractsManager.t.sol`)
- `mise x -- just test-dev --match-path test/L2/CrossL2Inbox.t.sol` — 18 passed
- `mise x -- just test-dev --match-path test/L1/L1EventRegistry.t.sol` — 7 passed
- clean default-profile source build, interface check, snapshot generation, formatting, pragma, unused-import, spacer, reinitializer, semver, and test-structure checks pass
